summary.mechanism_note: Loss-of-autoinhibition, not a novel gain-of-function. Full-length BRAF is held inactive by an intramolecular clamp: CR1 (the RAS-binding and cysteine-rich domains) together with CR2 (containing the S365 14-3-3 docking site) restrain the CR3 kinase domain until active RAS displaces them. The KIAA1549::BRAF fusion deletes CR1 and CR2 while preserving CR3 (exons 11-18) intact, leaving a pre-activated kinase that homodimerizes and signals to MEK/ERK independently of upstream RAS -- the same RAS-independent, dimer-dependent ("class II") activation state as BRAF V600E, reached structurally instead of by point mutation. The truncation itself is sufficient: unlike EML4-ALK-style fusions, BRAF fusions do not require a dimerization motif from the partner -- at least eight structurally unrelated 5' partners are interchangeable, consistent with the partner's role being deletion of the regulatory region rather than supplying a dimerization domain of its own.

Summary.genomic_vs_protein_clustering_note: The 2 events sharing protein position 380 aa use 2 distinct genomic positions spanning 4081 bp -- the protein-position recurrence is broader than any single genomic hotspot, consistent with independent intronic breakpoints mapped (or clamped) onto the same protein/exon boundary rather than one shared DNA lesion.

Summary.null_model: breakpoints uniform across the gene's genomic span, role kept
Summary.panel_capture_caveat: The random-breakage null assumes a breakpoint anywhere in the gene would be detected. Capture panels such as MSK-IMPACT tile only selected introns, so concentration on panel data is partly by assay design and this p-value overstates the evidence for biological concentration. Confirm in a cohort sequenced without intron selection (whole genome or RNA).
